subject: English
title: A Bottle of Dew — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: What does Rama Natha believe the magic potion can do?
questions.explanation: Rama Natha wanted to get rich quickly, so he dreamt of a potion that turns things into gold.

questions.text: What does Rama Natha have to collect?
questions.explanation: He was told the potion needed dew from banana leaves, so he planted and cared for many banana plants.

questions.text: How does the family actually become successful?
questions.explanation: All those banana plants gave fruit, and selling the bananas made the family wealthy.

questions.text: What is the main lesson of the story?
options: Hard work and perseverance matter more than shortcuts
questions.explanation: The real 'magic' was years of hard work, not a potion.

questions.text: Who helps sell the bananas?
questions.explanation: Madhumati, Rama Natha's wife, took the bananas to the market and sold them.

subject: English
title: The Unlikely Best Friends — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Why is Gajaraj unhappy despite being well cared for?
options: He wants to leave the kingdom
He has no friend to play with
questions.explanation: Gajaraj had food and care, but he was lonely.

questions.text: Who enters the stable one evening?
questions.explanation: A stray dog wandered into the elephant's stable.

questions.text: What does Gajaraj notice about the dog?
options: It is looking for the king
It is injured by a hunter
questions.explanation: The dog was weak and hungry, which made Gajaraj care for it.

questions.text: What is the main idea of the chapter?
options: Only similar animals can be friends
Comfort is more important than friendship
questions.explanation: An elephant and a dog became best friends - friends do not have to be alike.

questions.text: Which quality is most important in the friendship?
questions.explanation: Their friendship grew because they were kind to and cared for each other.

subject: English
title: The Raven and the Fox — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: What was Mr Raven holding in his beak?
options: A morsel (a small piece of food)
questions.explanation: The poem says the Raven held 'a morsel the Fox would go far to seek' in his beak.

questions.text: What is the Fox called in the poem?
questions.explanation: The poem calls him 'Reynard the Fox'.

questions.text: How did the Fox get the food?
options: He praised the Raven and asked him to sing, so the food fell
He climbed the tree and grabbed it
He asked politely and the Raven shared it
questions.explanation: When the proud Raven opened his beak to sing, the morsel dropped to the Fox.

questions.text: What lesson does the poem teach?
options: Never sit on a tree branch
Do not let flattery and pride fool you
questions.explanation: The Fox says: 'Ignore sweet words that make you glow. Pride, my friend, is rather unwise.'

questions.text: In 'great big beak', the words 'big' and 'beak' begin with the same sound. This is called
questions.explanation: Repeating the same consonant sound at the start of nearby words is alliteration.

subject: English
title: Rama to the Rescue — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Who is Rama in the story?
questions.explanation: Rama is the kotwal - the person who guards the village and catches thieves.

questions.text: Why could the man and his wife not fall asleep?
options: They heard someone trying to get into the house
questions.explanation: They heard a noise - a thief was digging his way into their house.

questions.text: How did the couple call the kotwal without making the thief suspicious?
options: The man ran to the kotwal's house
The wife called out 'Rama' loudly, as if choosing a name for their child
questions.explanation: Pretending to talk about naming their child, the wife called 'Rama' louder and louder until the kotwal heard his name and came.

questions.text: Why did the thief keep quiet and listen to the couple?
options: He was waiting for the kotwal
He was too sleepy to move
He wanted to know their child's name
He hoped they would say where their money and jewels were kept
questions.explanation: The thief thought, 'Perhaps they are talking about their money,' so he waited to hear more.

questions.text: What is the full form of 'they're'?
questions.explanation: The apostrophe in a contraction shows a missing letter: they're = they are.

questions.text: How does the poet feel about having special friends?
questions.explanation: She says, 'With special friends I feel I'm blessed.'

questions.text: What does the poet want to use to 'see' what friends can be?
questions.explanation: 'Let me use my heart to see, to realise what friends can be.'

questions.text: What does 'love my friends the way they are' mean?
options: Only love friends when they are happy
Accept friends as they are, without judging them
questions.explanation: The poet wants to 'make no judgements from afar' and accept her friends fully.

questions.text: Why can we call this poem a prayer?
options: It is sung only in a temple
The poet asks to become a better friend, with lines like 'May my...' and 'Let me...'
questions.explanation: A prayer is a wish or request; the whole poem asks to be a good, caring friend.

questions.text: A friend who stands by you even when you make a mistake is
questions.explanation: Being loyal means staying faithful to a friend in good and bad times.

questions.text: What did Mario's grandfather bet him?
questions.explanation: Grandpa bet a fruit chaat that Mario did not have as many real friends as he thought.

questions.text: What was special about the chair grandfather gave Mario?
questions.explanation: Grandpa said it was a special invisible chair, so it was tricky to sit on.

questions.text: Who held Mario up so that he would not fall?
questions.explanation: Mario's three real friends held him up while the others laughed.

questions.text: What did Mario learn from the chair test?
options: Friends should laugh when we fall
True friends care for us and do not enjoy our bad luck
Having many friends is all that matters
questions.explanation: The 'magic' showed who cared: real friends helped, others only made fun of him.

questions.text: In the word 'friendly', the part '-ly' is called a
questions.explanation: Letters added after a root word (friend) to make a new word are a suffix.

questions.text: Who gave the tree the name 'Neem'?
questions.explanation: Neem Baba says its Sanskrit names were Arishta, Nimba and Nimbaca, and 'Neem' was given by the Iranians.

questions.text: Why were neem leaves put on the bed of a child with measles?
options: They destroy germs and give relief from itching
They make the child sleep faster
questions.explanation: Neem leaves have chemical properties that destroy germs and stop them from breeding.

questions.text: How does neem seed powder help farmers?
options: It changes the colour of crops
It keeps locusts and termites away from crops
questions.explanation: Sprayed on plants, it stops locusts eating them, and it protects crops from termites.

questions.text: Why is furniture made from neem wood useful?
questions.explanation: Neem Baba says furniture made from neem wood is not eaten by termites.

questions.text: Amber talks to the neem tree as if it were a person. This is called
questions.explanation: Giving human qualities to a non-human thing is personification.

subject: English
title: What a Bird Thought — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: When the bird was inside the egg, what did it think the world was made of?
questions.explanation: 'I thought the world was small and round, and made of pale, blue shell.'

questions.text: When the bird lived in the nest, what did it think the world was made of?
questions.explanation: Its nest was made of straw, so that was the whole world it knew.

questions.text: Why did the bird later think the world was made of leaves?
options: It was born on a leaf
It fluttered out of the nest and saw leaves all around
questions.explanation: Out of the nest, the bird could see the leaves it had never noticed before.

questions.text: What does the bird say at the end, after flying beyond the tree?
options: The world is made of straw
The world is small and round
It does not know how the world is made
questions.explanation: 'I don't know how the world is made, and neither do my neighbours.'

questions.text: What is the poem mainly about?
options: How our idea of the world grows as we see more of it
questions.explanation: Shell, then nest, then leaves, then beyond: each time the bird sees more, its idea of the world changes.

subject: English
title: Spices that Heal Us — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: What is haldi called in English?
questions.explanation: Daadi starts her letter with haldi, which is called turmeric in English.

questions.text: Daadi soaks a spice overnight and drinks the water to keep her sugar level and weight in control. Which spice?
questions.explanation: She soaks methi seeds overnight and drinks the water in the morning.

questions.text: Which spices give relief from toothache until we can see a dentist?
questions.explanation: Daadi writes that cinnamon and clove give relief from toothache.

questions.text: Why are saunf and ajwain served at the end of a meal?
questions.explanation: Fennel and carom seeds help in the digestion of food.

questions.text: From whom did Daadi learn these home remedies?
questions.explanation: 'When I was a child, I learnt them from my grandmother.'

questions.text: What was Prabhat's problem at the start of the story?
questions.explanation: Prabhat would only play when he was sure of winning.

questions.text: How did Prabhat win the badminton match against Surya?
options: The coach gave him extra points
By changing the scoreboard when Surya was not looking
questions.explanation: Prabhat was keeping score, and he cheated while Surya looked elsewhere.

questions.text: How did Surya react to losing?
options: He did not mind and said it had been fun
questions.explanation: Surya said, 'It's been fun. We should play again some other time.'

questions.text: What did Prabhat notice when Surya played basketball?
options: Surya enjoyed the game even though he could not score
Surya did not play at all
questions.explanation: Surya could not score a basket for ten minutes, yet he kept smiling and enjoying it.

questions.text: What does the title 'Change of Heart' refer to?
options: Prabhat learning to enjoy games instead of only wanting to win
questions.explanation: By watching Surya, Prabhat learnt sporting spirit - enjoying the game for its own sake.

questions.text: Where do the children play ball?
options: Next to the creek in a neighbour's field
questions.explanation: 'Evenings, we play ball next to the creek in our neighbour's field.'

questions.text: What is a 'creek'?
questions.explanation: A creek is a small body of flowing water.

questions.text: Why can't the speaker 'catch her breath'?
options: She has been running very fast
questions.explanation: 'We run so fast I can't even catch my breath.'

questions.text: Who is 'the winner' in the poem?
questions.explanation: The poem ends: 'game's over. Night wins!'

questions.text: Why does Night 'win'?
options: It gets dark, so the time for play is over
The children are tired of the game
questions.explanation: When the sky turns from blue to black, the children have to stop playing.

subject: English
title: Yoga—A Way of Life — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: The word 'Yoga' comes from the Sanskrit root 'yuj'. What does 'yuj' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Yuj' means to join - the unity of mind and body, thought and action.

questions.text: Who presented yoga in a systematic way in the 'Yoga Sutras'?
questions.explanation: Sage Patanjali described yoga as a way to make the mind quiet and free from distractions.

questions.text: Which of these is a benefit of yoga given in the chapter?
options: It replaces the need for sleep
It removes the need to eat
It calms the mind and reduces stress
questions.explanation: Breathing and meditation in yoga calm the mind, reduce stress and improve sleep.

questions.text: What did the World Health Organisation launch in June 2021 to help people practise yoga?
questions.explanation: WHO launched the free mYoga app with videos and audio to support yoga practice.

questions.text: Why should yoga be practised without distractions?
options: Yoga can only be done alone
The mind has to be with the body in each posture
It must be done in silence by law
questions.explanation: Each stretch should be coordinated with breath and awareness.

questions.text: What is the 'Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat' programme about?
options: Knowing we all belong to one nation and celebrating unity in diversity
questions.explanation: Renu explains it is about the bond of one nation and our unity in diversity.

questions.text: Aipan, drawn with white rice-flour paste on brick-red walls, is a folk art from
questions.explanation: Aakansha from Uttarakhand describes Aipan, drawn by women for family functions and festivals.

questions.text: In Dhokra metal craft from Odisha, what is melted and poured into the empty space?
questions.explanation: The wax melts out, then melted brass takes its place and the shape of the wax.

questions.text: Kondapalli toys from Andhra Pradesh are made from
questions.explanation: Balamurali says soft wood from nearby hills is carved and joined with 'makku' paste.

questions.text: Which word shows the last step in a process?
questions.explanation: Words like first, next, then and finally show the order of steps.

questions.text: What does the poet compare the kites to?
questions.explanation: 'See the kites fly, like coloured birds in the wind-whipped sky.'

questions.text: 'Like coloured birds' and 'light as air' compare things using 'like' and 'as'. This is called
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using 'like' or 'as'.

questions.text: Why does the child wish to be small and light as air?
options: To climb on a kite and sail up in the sky
questions.explanation: 'I wish I were small and light as air, I would climb on a kite and sail up there.'

questions.text: From the kite, what would the child look down on?
options: The park and the rooftops of town
questions.explanation: 'What fun it would be to look right down, over the park and the rooftops of town.'

questions.text: Why are the words 'high, high' repeated in the last stanza?
options: To show the wind has stopped
Because the poet forgot the line
To show that the kite is flying very high
To show the kite is falling
questions.explanation: Repeating a word adds emphasis - the kite is very high in the air.

subject: English
title: Ila Sachani: Embroidering Dreams with her Feet — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Ila Sachani is famous for which style of embroidery?
questions.explanation: She is very good at Kathiawar embroidery, a style from Gujarat that needs a lot of skill.

questions.text: How does Ila Sachani do her embroidery?
questions.explanation: She was born unable to use her hands in the usual way, so she learnt to embroider with her feet.

questions.text: Who taught Ila the art of embroidery?
questions.explanation: Her mother and grandmother were skilled in Kathiawar embroidery and taught her.

questions.text: What 'opened new doors' for Ila?
options: Her work was displayed at a state exhibition
questions.explanation: The government office in Surat displayed her embroidery, people bought it, and she became famous.

questions.text: What is the main message of Ila's story?
options: Only people with two hands can make art
Challenges can be turned into victories with hard work and never giving up
questions.explanation: Ila became a celebrated artist and received the President's Medal through determination.

questions.text: When was the National War Memorial in New Delhi established?
questions.explanation: It was established in February 2019 by the Government of India.

questions.text: Why was the National War Memorial built?
options: To show the history of kings
questions.explanation: It is a national monument built in honour of the soldiers who served the country.

questions.text: According to the poem, what glows in silence at the memorial?
questions.explanation: 'The eternal flame, in silence it glows, paying homage to their courage.'

questions.text: What does the poem say is etched at the memorial?
questions.explanation: 'Each name etched, each stone, each story to confide.'

questions.text: 'From battle fields to skies, and to oceans wide' - where do our soldiers serve?
options: On land, in the skies and at sea
questions.explanation: The line covers soldiers on land, in the air and at sea, standing for Bharat side by side.

questions.text: What comes next in 1, 3, 5, 7, ...?
questions.explanation: These are the odd numbers; each one is 2 more than the last, so 7 + 2 = 9.

questions.text: Which sequence is made of square numbers?
questions.explanation: 1, 4, 9, 16 are 1x1, 2x2, 3x3 and 4x4, and can be drawn as squares of dots.

questions.text: Which sequence is made of triangular numbers?
questions.explanation: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 dots can each be arranged as a triangle.

questions.text: What is most important when studying a number sequence?
questions.explanation: Once you know the rule, you can continue the sequence and explain why it works.

questions.text: Why do pictures help with number patterns?
options: They remove the need for rules
They make mathematical relationships easier to see
They always give the answer instantly
questions.explanation: Drawing numbers as shapes, like squares and triangles of dots, shows why a pattern works.

questions.text: What is the common endpoint of the two rays that form an angle called?
questions.explanation: The two arms (rays) of an angle meet at its vertex.

questions.text: Which extends endlessly in both directions?
questions.explanation: A line goes on forever both ways; a ray only one way; a line segment has two endpoints.

questions.text: How many endpoints does a line segment have?
questions.explanation: A line segment starts and stops at two endpoints.

questions.text: How many right angles make a straight angle?
questions.explanation: A straight angle is half a turn and a right angle is a quarter turn, so two right angles make a straight angle.

questions.text: Why is careful naming important in geometry?
options: Different names can refer to different points or angles
questions.explanation: A clear name like angle PQR tells everyone exactly which angle we mean.

questions.text: Which of these numbers is a palindrome?
questions.explanation: A palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards: 5-7-5.

questions.text: In the 'supercells' activity, a cell is a supercell when
options: its number is greater than all the numbers in its neighbouring cells
it is in the middle of the table
questions.explanation: Neighbours are the cells to the left, right, top and bottom; a supercell beats all of them.

questions.text: Kaprekar's routine (largest arrangement of the digits minus the smallest, repeated) on a 4-digit number with different digits always reaches
questions.explanation: D. R. Kaprekar, a teacher from Devlali, Maharashtra, found this 'magic number' 6174.

questions.text: In a Collatz sequence, what do you do when the number is odd?
questions.explanation: Even numbers are halved; odd numbers become 3 x n + 1. No one has proved the sequence always reaches 1.

questions.text: What is the digit sum of 4,568?
questions.explanation: Add the digits: 4 + 5 + 6 + 8 = 23.

subject: Mathematics
title: Data Handling and Presentation — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Facts, numbers, measures or observations that give us information are called
questions.explanation: Any collection of facts, numbers or observations that convey information is called data.

questions.text: In tally marks, how is a count of 5 shown?
options: Four lines with a fifth line drawn across them
questions.explanation: When the count reaches 5, a line is drawn through the previous four, which makes counting by fives easy.

questions.text: In a pictograph, one picture stands for 5 students. How many students do 4 pictures show?
questions.explanation: The scale says each picture = 5, so 4 pictures = 4 x 5 = 20.

questions.text: A bar graph with vertical bars is also called a
questions.explanation: Vertical bars stand like columns, so it is called a column graph.

questions.text: When drawing a bar graph, the bars should have
options: the same width and equal gaps between them
questions.explanation: Only the length or height of a bar should show the number; everything else stays the same.

questions.text: Numbers that have exactly two factors (1 and the number itself) are called
questions.explanation: A prime number has only two factors, for example 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11.

questions.text: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 29 has only the factors 1 and 29. But 21 = 3 x 7, 27 = 3 x 9 and 33 = 3 x 11.

questions.text: Which pair of numbers is co-prime?
questions.explanation: Co-prime numbers have no common factor other than 1. 4 and 9 share only 1; 15 and 39 share 3.

questions.text: What is the prime factorisation of 56?
questions.explanation: In a prime factorisation every factor must be prime: 56 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 7.

questions.text: To check whether a number is divisible by 4, you only need to look at
options: the number formed by its last two digits
questions.explanation: If the last two digits form a multiple of 4, the whole number is divisible by 4.

questions.text: The perimeter of a closed figure is
options: the length of its longest side
questions.explanation: Perimeter is the distance covered when you go once around the boundary.

questions.text: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2 x (length + breadth) = 2 x (8 + 5) = 26 cm.

questions.text: A square has sides of 6 cm. What is its perimeter?
questions.explanation: Perimeter of a square = 4 x side = 4 x 6 = 24 cm.

questions.text: A floor is 5 m long and 4 m wide. What is its area?
questions.explanation: Area = length x width = 5 m x 4 m = 20 square metres. Area is measured in square units.

questions.text: A diagonal cuts a rectangle into two triangles. The area of each triangle is
options: double the area of the rectangle
half the area of the rectangle
equal to the area of the rectangle
a quarter of the area of the rectangle
questions.explanation: The two triangles are identical and together make the rectangle, so each is half of it.

questions.text: One roti is shared equally among 4 children. How much does each child get?
questions.explanation: Dividing one whole into 4 equal parts gives each part 1/4.

questions.text: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/3?
questions.explanation: Multiplying the top and bottom by 2 gives 4/6, which is the same length on the number line.

questions.text: What is 12/16 in its simplest form?
questions.explanation: Divide top and bottom by 4, their largest common factor: 12/16 = 3/4.

questions.text: How is 7/2 written as a mixed fraction?
questions.explanation: 7 halves = 6 halves + 1 half = 3 wholes and 1/2.

questions.text: What is 1/3 + 1/6?
questions.explanation: Use a common unit, as in Brahmagupta's method: 1/3 = 2/6, so 2/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2.

questions.text: The distance from the centre of a circle to any point on the circle is called the
questions.explanation: Fixing a radius on the compass lets you draw a circle around the centre.

questions.text: Every point on a circle is
options: at the same distance from its centre
at a different distance from the centre
questions.explanation: That is exactly what makes a circle: all its points are equally far from the centre.

questions.text: Which is true for every rectangle?
options: All sides are equal and no angle is 90 degrees
Opposite sides are equal and all angles are 90 degrees
All four sides are always different
questions.explanation: A rectangle has opposite sides equal (R1) and all angles equal to 90 degrees (R2).

questions.text: Which is true for every square?
options: All sides are equal and all angles are 90 degrees
questions.explanation: A square has all sides equal (S1) and all angles 90 degrees (S2).

questions.text: A line joining opposite corners of a rectangle is called a
questions.explanation: Joining P to R and Q to S in rectangle PQRS gives its two diagonals.

questions.text: A line of symmetry is a line
options: along which a figure can be folded so the two parts exactly overlap
that cuts a figure into two different parts
that is the longest side of a figure
questions.explanation: If both halves match perfectly when folded, the fold line is a line of symmetry.

questions.text: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
questions.explanation: A square can be folded vertically, horizontally and along both diagonals: 4 lines.

questions.text: A paper windmill has no line of symmetry, but it looks the same after a quarter turn. This is called
questions.explanation: A figure that looks exactly the same after turning by less than a full turn has rotational symmetry.

questions.text: Which angle is an angle of symmetry for every figure?
questions.explanation: After a full turn of 360 degrees, any figure is back in its original position.

questions.text: The windmill looks the same after turns of 90, 180, 270 and 360 degrees. How many angles of symmetry does it have?
questions.explanation: Each of those four turns is an angle of symmetry.

subject: Mathematics
title: The Other Side of Zero — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Positive numbers, negative numbers and zero together are called
Which is greater: -3 or -7?
questions.explanation: On the number line -3 is to the right of -7 (closer to zero), so -3 is greater.

questions.text: Using tokens, what is (+5) + (-3)?
questions.explanation: Each positive and negative token make a zero pair. Remove 3 zero pairs and 2 positive tokens are left.
Subtracting a negative number is the same as adding the positive: (+6) + (+9) = +15.

questions.text: In a bank passbook, a debit (money taken out) can be thought of as
questions.explanation: Credits add money (positive); debits take it away (negative).

subject: Science
title: The Wonderful World of Science — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: How does the chapter describe science?
options: A way of thinking, observing and doing things to understand the world
A list of facts to memorise
Only experiments done in a laboratory
questions.explanation: Science is a way of thinking, observing and doing things to understand the world we live in.

questions.text: What often starts a scientific investigation?
questions.explanation: We first observe something interesting or something we do not understand, and ask about it.

questions.text: Your pen stops writing and you guess the ink has finished. What should you do next?
options: Test the guess, for example by checking the ink refill
questions.explanation: Scientists test their guesses; if the refill is empty, the guess was correct.

questions.text: What do scientists do after an experiment?
questions.explanation: The results show whether the guess was right or needs to change.

questions.text: Which quality does the chapter say is most important for learning science?
questions.explanation: Being curious and observing your surroundings keenly comes first - the textbook is even named 'Curiosity'.

subject: Science
title: Diversity in the Living World — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Why do living things have different features?
options: Their features help them survive in different environments
questions.explanation: Living things have features suited to where they live.

questions.text: The special features that help plants and animals survive in a particular region are called
questions.explanation: Camels in the cold desert of Ladakh grow long hair on the head and neck to survive the cold winters.

questions.text: The place where a plant or animal lives is called its
questions.explanation: Plants and animals can be grouped by their habitats, like deserts, mountains or water.

questions.text: Which body part helps a fish move through water?
questions.explanation: Fins and a streamlined body are adaptations for moving in water.

questions.text: Why is grouping living things useful?
options: It helps us understand their diversity
questions.explanation: Grouping by shared features makes the huge variety of life easier to study.

subject: Science
title: Mindful Eating: A Path to a Healthy Body — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: In the iodine test, which colour shows that starch is present?
questions.explanation: A blue-black colour after adding dilute iodine solution indicates starch.

questions.text: In the test for proteins, what colour shows that protein is present?
questions.explanation: A violet colour in the test tube indicates the presence of proteins.

questions.text: How do you test a food item for fats?
options: Heat it until it turns violet
Press it in paper and look for an oily patch
Add iodine and look for a blue-black colour
Mix it with salt and water
questions.explanation: Fat leaves an oily patch on paper that does not dry away.

questions.text: Bleeding and swollen gums (scurvy) are caused by a lack of
questions.explanation: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C; lemons and oranges help cure it.

questions.text: A balanced diet is one that has
options: all essential nutrients, roughage and water in the right amounts
questions.explanation: A balanced diet supports proper growth by giving the body everything it needs in the right amount.

questions.text: Which of these will a magnet attract?
questions.explanation: Iron is a magnetic material; wood, plastic and glass are non-magnetic.

questions.text: Where do most iron filings stick on a magnet?
questions.explanation: The attraction of a magnet is strongest at its two poles.

questions.text: What happens when the North poles of two magnets are brought close?
questions.explanation: Like poles (N-N or S-S) repel; unlike poles (N-S) attract.

questions.text: A freely suspended bar magnet always comes to rest along which direction?
questions.explanation: The Earth itself behaves like a giant magnet; the magnetic compass works on this idea.

questions.text: If a magnet is broken into two pieces, each piece
options: still has both a North pole and a South pole
questions.explanation: North and South poles always exist in pairs, even in the smallest piece of a magnet.

subject: Science
title: Measurement of Length and Motion — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: The children measured the same table with their handspans and got different answers. Why?
options: Their handspans were of different lengths
Handspans always give the same answer
questions.explanation: Body parts vary from person to person, which is why we need standard units.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of length?
questions.explanation: The International System of Units (SI) uses the metre for length; 1 m = 100 cm.

questions.text: Where should your eye be when you read a length on a scale?
options: Directly above the point being measured
To the left of the point
To the right of the point
questions.explanation: Looking from the side gives a wrong reading.

questions.text: A heavy box pushed along a straight path shows
questions.explanation: Motion along a straight line is called linear motion.

questions.text: A child on a swing moving to and fro shows
questions.explanation: To-and-fro motion is oscillatory. Like circular motion, it repeats, so it is periodic.

questions.text: Materials through which we can see things clearly are called
questions.explanation: Glass, water and air are transparent.

questions.text: Butter paper and frosted glass are examples of
questions.explanation: Through translucent materials we can see objects, but not clearly.

questions.text: Which of these is opaque?
questions.explanation: We cannot see through opaque materials like wood, cardboard and metals.

questions.text: Materials with shiny surfaces, usually metals, are said to be
questions.explanation: Lustre is the shine of metals; it is clearest on a freshly cut surface.

questions.text: Sugar mixes completely and disappears in water. We say sugar is
questions.explanation: Materials that dissolve in water are soluble; those that do not, like sand, are insoluble.

subject: Science
title: Temperature and its Measurement — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Which thermometer is used to measure human body temperature?
questions.explanation: Clinical thermometers are for body temperature; laboratory thermometers are for other uses.

questions.text: The normal temperature of a healthy human body is taken to be
questions.explanation: 37.0 degrees C is the average for many healthy people; a healthy person may be slightly different.

questions.text: Why can't a clinical thermometer measure the temperature of boiling water?
options: Boiling water is outside its range
questions.explanation: Body temperature normally stays between 35 and 42 degrees C, so that is all a clinical thermometer covers.

questions.text: What is the range of the laboratory thermometer shown in the chapter?
questions.explanation: A laboratory thermometer covers a much wider range than a clinical one.

questions.text: Why are mercury thermometers being replaced by digital thermometers?
options: Mercury is toxic and hard to dispose of if the thermometer breaks
Mercury thermometers cannot show degrees Celsius
questions.explanation: Digital thermometers have no mercury, and their display is easier to read.

subject: Science
title: A Journey through States of Water — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: The change of water into water vapour is called
questions.explanation: Evaporation happens all the time, even at room temperature.

questions.text: Drops of water appear on the outside of a glass of ice-cold water. Why?
options: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold glass
questions.explanation: Condensation is water vapour changing back into liquid water.

questions.text: The change from a liquid into a solid is called
questions.explanation: Freezing turns liquid to solid; melting turns solid to liquid.

questions.text: Where does water evaporate faster?
options: In shade rather than in sunlight
At the same speed in both
In sunlight rather than in shade
questions.explanation: Water evaporates faster from the cap kept in sunlight than from the one in shade.

questions.text: Why does water stay cool in an earthen pot (matka)?
options: Matka water has salt in it
Water seeps through the pot and evaporates, which cools it
questions.explanation: Evaporation takes heat away, giving a cooling effect - the idea behind a pot-in-pot cooler.

subject: Science
title: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Separating tea leaves from tea with a strainer is called
questions.explanation: A strainer, cloth or filter paper lets liquid through and holds back the solid bits.

questions.text: Separating grains from their stalks is called
questions.explanation: Threshing beats the stalks so the grains come off; threshers do it by machine.

questions.text: Separating light husk from heavier grain using wind or blowing air is called
questions.explanation: The wind blows the lighter husk away while the heavier grain falls nearby.

questions.text: After mud settles at the bottom of a glass, the clear water is poured off by tilting the glass. This pouring off is called
questions.explanation: Settling of the heavy mud is sedimentation; pouring off the liquid is decantation.

questions.text: Which method is used to get butter from curd?
questions.explanation: Churning curd with a churner (mathni) separates the butter.

subject: Science
title: Living Creatures: Exploring their Characteristics — Chapter Quiz

questions.text: Which of these is true of all living beings?
questions.explanation: Living beings grow, move, breathe, excrete, reproduce and respond to stimuli.

questions.text: Stepping on a thorn and touching a hot object are examples of
questions.explanation: A stimulus is anything that makes a living being respond; plants respond to stimuli too.

questions.text: Removing waste products from the body is called
questions.explanation: Animals excrete urine; plants can give out excess water and minerals as droplets on leaves.

questions.text: Larva and pupa are stages in the life cycle of a
questions.explanation: A mosquito goes from egg to larva to pupa to adult. A frog has tadpole and froglet stages instead.

questions.text: In the germination activity, which seeds germinate?
options: Seeds with air but no water
Seeds that get both air and water
Seeds with water but no air
questions.explanation: Air and water are essential conditions for a seed to germinate.

questions.text: Resources we get from nature, such as air, water and sunlight, are called
questions.explanation: Air, water, sunlight, forests, soil, rocks, minerals and fossil fuels are all natural resources.

questions.text: Which of these is a renewable natural resource?
questions.explanation: Renewable resources like air, water and forests are restored within a reasonable time.

questions.text: Why are coal and petroleum called non-renewable?
options: They take millions of years to form
questions.explanation: Once used up, they cannot be replaced within a reasonable time.

questions.text: Fossil fuels were formed from
options: remains of microorganisms and plants buried deep inside the earth
questions.explanation: Over millions of years, buried remains changed into coal, petroleum and natural gas.

questions.text: What can windmills be used for?
options: Generating electricity, pulling up water and running flour mills
questions.explanation: Moving air (wind) turns the wings of a windmill, just as it turns a firki.

questions.text: Groups of stars that form patterns in the sky were earlier called
questions.explanation: Orion (the hunter) and Ursa Major are examples of constellations.

questions.text: Which star appears nearly stationary in the north?
questions.explanation: The Pole Star is part of the Little Dipper and helps find the north direction.

questions.text: In India, the Big Dipper is known as
questions.explanation: The Big Dipper (Saptarishi) lies in the constellation Ursa Major.

questions.text: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite. About how long does it take to go around the Earth once?
questions.explanation: Objects that move around planets are satellites; the Moon takes about 27 days per revolution.

questions.text: The asteroid belt lies between the paths of which two planets?
questions.explanation: Many asteroids revolve around the Sun in this region between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.text: ఈ పాఠంలో ప్రధానంగా ఎవరి శ్రమను గౌరవిస్తారు?
questions.explanation: ‘అభినందన’ పాఠం రైతులు, సైనికులు వంటి కష్టపడి పనిచేసే వారి సేవను గుర్తు చేస్తుంది.

questions.text: రైతు ప్రధానంగా ఏ పని చేస్తాడు?
questions.explanation: రైతు వర్షం, ఎండ ఉన్నా పొలంలో శ్రమించి పంటను పండిస్తాడు.

questions.text: సైనికుల ప్రధాన బాధ్యత ఏమిటి?
questions.explanation: సైనికులు దేశాన్ని కాపాడుతారు; వారి ధైర్యం, క్రమశిక్షణ మనకు ప్రేరణ.

questions.text: పాఠం మనకు ఏమి నేర్పుతుంది?
questions.explanation: వారి శ్రమను గుర్తించి గౌరవించడం మన బాధ్యత అని పాఠం చెబుతుంది.

questions.text: కథలోని స్నేహితులు ఏమి చేస్తారు?
questions.explanation: కాకి, ఎలుక, తాబేలు, జింక ఒకరికొకరు సహాయం చేసుకుంటూ మంచి స్నేహితులుగా ఉంటాయి.

questions.text: స్నేహం యొక్క ముఖ్య లక్షణం ఏది?
questions.explanation: నిజమైన స్నేహం అంటే కష్టసమయంలో తోడుగా నిలబడటం, నమ్మకం ఉంచడం.

questions.text: భిన్నమైన జంతువులు ఎందుకు కలిసి పనిచేస్తాయి?
questions.explanation: ప్రతి ఒక్కరి ప్రత్యేకమైన సామర్థ్యం సమూహానికి ఉపయోగపడుతుంది; కలిసి ఉంటే బలం.

questions.text: ఈ పాఠం ప్రధానంగా ఏ విలువను నేర్పుతుంది?
questions.explanation: స్నేహానికి రూపం, పరిమాణం లేదా జాతి అడ్డంకులు కావని ఈ కథ చూపిస్తుంది.
